about: Statutory limits on yearly growth of a home's assessed value, by state, read by the property tax bill when the catalog law capping property-tax growth is in force. A state absent here has no row yet and takes the generic estimate in reach-group-b-parameters.json (propertyTaxGrowthCapShare). Where a statute also limits growth to the CPI change, only the ceiling is read. The assessment is kept per household, so a buyer's household is always assessed afresh at market: right for the states whose cap resets on sale, and a known gap for Oregon and Arizona, whose limited values carry over to a buyer (resetOnSale false).

AR.source: Arkansas Constitution Amendment 79, sec. 1: a homestead's assessed value rises at most 5% a year (other real property 10%); the amendment lets the assessment follow market on a change of ownership.

AZ.source: Arizona Constitution art. IX, sec. 18 (Proposition 117): limited property value rises at most 5% a year.

CA.source: California Constitution art. XIII A, sec. 2 (Proposition 13): assessed value rises at most 2% a year; reassessed to market on a change in ownership or new construction.

FL.source: Florida Constitution art. VII, sec. 4(d) (Save Our Homes): homestead assessed value rises at most 3% or the CPI change, whichever is lower; reset to market on a change of ownership. The ceiling is read; the CPI limit is not.

MI.source: Michigan Constitution art. IX, sec. 3 (Proposal A): taxable value rises at most 5% or the CPI change, whichever is lower; uncapped on a transfer of ownership. The ceiling is read; the CPI limit is not.

NM.source: New Mexico Property Tax Code sec. 7-36-21.2: residential taxable value rises at most 3% a year; reset to market on a change of ownership.

NY.source: New York Real Property Tax Law sec. 1805: a Class 1 (residential) parcel's assessment rises at most 6% a year and 20% over five years, outside New York City's own class rules for increases from physical changes; reset to market is not applied on sale.

OK.source: Oklahoma Constitution art. X, sec. 8B: assessed value rises at most 3% a year; reset to market on a change of ownership.

OR.source: Oregon Constitution art. XI, sec. 11 (Measure 50): maximum assessed value rises at most 3% a year.

TX.source: Texas Tax Code sec. 23.23: a homestead's appraised value rises at most 10% a year (the 2023 law applies the cap to non-homestead property up to $5 million in the same way, not read here).
